## Problem

The `bedrock-spend-cap` Lambda can compute the spend guard from synthetic rates for Claude traffic. The warning threshold and deny-policy threshold then operate on a number that is not fully measured. The original description framed this as the dominant model family always reaching `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`; later read-only investigation narrowed and corrected that framing.

## Confirmed current root cause

`_normalise()` is not the root cause on `origin/main`. Lines 150-177 strip stacked dotted prefixes including `us.` and `anthropic.`, and the existing test at `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py` lines 768-773 asserts `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` normalises to `claudesonnet46`.

The empirical loader is the structural gap. `_refresh_rates()` queries Cost Explorer at lines 184-190 with `Filter={"Dimensions": {"Key": "SERVICE", "Values": ["Amazon Bedrock"]}}` and groups only by `USAGE_TYPE`. Investigation recorded on this ticket found that current Claude usage is billed under separate services such as `Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`, `Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`, `Claude Haiku 4.5 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`, and Opus equivalents. The query therefore cannot collect empirical Claude rates.

The second gap is the seed layer. `_seed_for()` matches seed needles by substring at lines 208-223. The configured seeds observed in investigation covered `claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-opus`, and `claude-sonnet-4-6`, but not `claude-sonnet-4-5`. As a result, `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` reached `_rate_for()`'s warning and fail-closed fallback at lines 273-274 across input, output, cache-read, and cache-write metrics.

## Preserved investigation findings

The stale-card theory was rejected: the rate card refresh day was current and populated. Pagination was rejected: the Cost Explorer response carried no `NextPageToken`. A post-load filter was rejected: the handler's exact `SERVICE == "Amazon Bedrock"` query shape returned no Claude usage-type groups at all, while grouping CE by `SERVICE` exposed positive Claude Bedrock Edition services.

The fallback direction was measured as over-pricing for the unseeded Sonnet 4.5 traffic, not under-pricing. Later comments also corrected the timing concern: the metered value tracks current CloudWatch token metrics and the handler intentionally computes spend from `max(cost_explorer, priced_tokens)` at lines 507-523. The Cost Explorer signal is slow by design; the fast governing signal is the priced CloudWatch meter.

The exposure is wider than one model. The active Claude workload is empirically unpriceable by the current CE service filter, so seeded models work only because static `SEED_RATES` happen to match them. Any future Claude model without a seed needle reaches the synthetic fallback until a human notices the warning log.

## Resolved design decisions

Fix the loader, not only the seed. Adding a `claude-sonnet-4-5` seed mitigates the current symptom, but it preserves the structural defect that no Claude Bedrock Edition service can refresh empirically. `_refresh_rates()` must include Claude Bedrock Edition services and retain enough service/model identity to map Cost Explorer usage groups back to CloudWatch `ModelId` values.

Handle Marketplace-style Claude usage types explicitly. Investigation found usage types shaped like `USE1-MP:USE1_InputTokenCount-Units`, while `_rate_for()` currently expects suffixes like `input-tokens` at lines 243-259. The fix must normalise those token-direction forms and convert units so the resulting rate is per 1,000 tokens like the rest of `TOKEN_METRICS`.

Expose synthetic participation. If any part of the metered spend uses `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K` or a static seed instead of an empirical rate, the handler response and persisted state must mark the figure as estimated. Fail-closed enforcement may still attach the deny policy on an estimated high value, but consumers must not read a synthetic component as a fully measured dollar figure.

## Testing seam

Add the tests to `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py`. Use the existing `FakeCE(results_by_time=...)`, `FakeAWS.client()`, and `load_handler()` seam at test lines 86-245. Extend `FakeCE` only as far as needed to assert the Cost Explorer query shape and return service-qualified groups; do not use live AWS.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_refresh_rates_collects_claude_bedrock_edition_services` feeds `FakeCE` one non-Claude `Amazon Bedrock` group and one `Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)` token group, then observes `_refresh_rates()` produce a Claude rate under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_refresh_rates_collects_claude_bedrock_edition_services`.
- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_refresh_rates_converts_marketplace_units_to_per_1k_tokens` feeds a `USE1-MP:USE1_InputTokenCount-Units` Claude group and observes a per-1,000-token rate rather than a per-1,000,000-token rate under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_refresh_rates_converts_marketplace_units_to_per_1k_tokens`.
- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_rate_for_claude_sonnet_45_uses_empirical_rate_before_fallback` calls `_rate_for("us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0", "InputTokenCount", rates)` with the refreshed Claude rate and observes that empirical rate, with no fail-closed fallback warning, under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_rate_for_claude_sonnet_45_uses_empirical_rate_before_fallback`.
- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_metered_spend_marks_seed_or_fallback_components_as_estimated` drives one seeded model and one fallback-priced model through `_metered_spend` and observes an estimated marker in the handler response and saved SSM state under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_metered_spend_marks_seed_or_fallback_components_as_estimated`.
- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_threshold_notifications_include_estimated_spend_marker` drives warning and deny-threshold branches with an estimated metered component and observes SNS text that names the estimate under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_threshold_notifications_include_estimated_spend_marker`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py` exits 0 with the new tests included.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.

## Testing

Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k 'refresh_rates_collects_claude_bedrock_edition_services or refresh_rates_converts_marketplace_units_to_per_1k_tokens or rate_for_claude_sonnet_45_uses_empirical_rate_before_fallback or metered_spend_marks_seed_or_fallback_components_as_estimated or threshold_notifications_include_estimated_spend_marker'` during development, then run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py`, and finally run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify` before push.

## Out of scope

This ticket does not change Terraform ownership of the live Lambda or redesign the spend guard around per-session attribution. Those findings were recorded as context, but the fix here is empirical rate discovery, unit normalisation, and estimate visibility inside the handler.
